correctness.rationale: A well-conditioned zonal block supplies orthonormal vectors with point values comparable to sqrt(N_k). Projecting the rotational Gaussian-beam tight frame onto the zonal orthogonal complement leaves an isotropic frame of dimension N_k-M; restricted invertibility supplies M well-conditioned projected beams whenever M/(N_k-M)<1, i.e. at every fixed density below 1/2. Mixing the two orthogonal blocks preserves the point peaks, while a sign choice preserves a uniform Gaussian-beam dual pairing. Hölder gives the low-p Sogge exponent and point propagation gives the high-p exponent.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Han's 2026 paper constructs density arbitrarily close to one separately on the high-p and low-p branches and explicitly uses different zonal and Gaussian-beam mechanisms. Searches for a common positive-density orthonormal family simultaneously saturating both branches and all exponents did not locate this statement. Residual risk remains because the synthesis is short and the source preprint is very recent.

value.rationale: The result produces a single orthonormal family of every fixed density rho<1/2 that is sharp for every Sogge Lp exponent simultaneously. It demonstrates coexistence, at positive density, of the point-concentration and geodesic-concentration mechanisms underlying the two classical branches, rather than merely branchwise abundance in different orthonormal systems.
